description:
Bring your friends, family, signs, flags, and all your Montco pride. This is our time to show up—for our towns, our state, and our country.

EAGLEVILLE
Wed, June 4th
5-7pm
Park & Ridge Ave

June 4th is just a couple days before the anniversary of D-Day and at this action, we honor those who stood up against tyranny by standing up ourselves. The battle for democracy didn’t end in history books—it’s here, now, in our streets and our neighborhoods.

We will also be collecting donations for Martha’s Choice Marketplace.  The most needed items are feminine hygiene products, diapers, and canned tuna.  Please donate if you are able.

About the CFC People's Neighborhood Protest Series:
The People’s Neighborhood Protests are a rotating series of local demonstrations taking place weekly across Montgomery County. —bringing visibility, voice, and collective resistance to the neighborhoods we live in. These peaceful, high-visibility actions happen during weekday rush hour (5–7 PM) and are designed to meet people where they are—right in their neighborhoods. Protest locations rotate weekly to cover different areas of the county, with the goal of sustaining momentum, building local connections, and expanding our movement block by block.

title: Flood the Zone with Candidates: Run for Everything! and Blue Horizon Chillhouse at the Rural Summit
description:

This hands-on session is for county chairs, local activists, current candidates, and anyone thinking about running for office. 

We’ll dig into how to:

title: NO KINGS Citizens' Parade - Wilmington, Delaware
description:
Hosted by Indivisible Highlands and Beyond; co-hosted with 302 United and Delaware Working Families Power.

Come out for Wilmington’s "No Kings Citizens' Parade" as part of the June 14th National Day of Defiance to counter Trump's ridiculous $45 million birthday parade in DC on this same day. Join us as we parade down Wilmington's own Pennsylvania Avenue to say "NO KINGS!"

June 14th is Flag Day and also the 250th birthday of the army — a day that marks when Americans first organized to stand up to a king. "Trump isn’t honoring that legacy. He’s hijacking it to celebrate himself."

“This country doesn’t belong to a king — and we’re not letting him throw himself a parade funded by tens of millions of our taxpayer dollars while stealing from us and stripping away our rights, our freedoms, and the programs our families rely on. On June 14th, we’re coming together to send one clear message: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.”

We will gather at the corner of Pennsylvania Avenue and N. Bancroft Parkway in Wilmington. Specifically, we'll meet on grass lawn between the two sides of N. Bancroft Parkway - on the Wawaset Park side of PA Ave., between PA Ave. and W. 11th St. - and march/walk on the sidewalk along Pennsylvania Avenue toward Tower Hill School.

A short rally (with music and guest speakers) will precede the parade. The full roundtrip march is 1.3 miles long.

Bring flags and signs (two-sided, if possible) as well as kazoos, drums, cowbells, etc.

If walking isn't possible for you, please come anyway - with signs and flags - and be part of a Honk and Wave rally along Pennsylvania Ave.

Parking is available on N. Bancroft Parkway and surrounding streets.

Given our commitment to nonviolent action, we expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. If you encounter a heckler or counter-protester (organized or unorganized, from a simple raised finger to a verbal taunt), the rule of thumb is to IGNORE IT!! Do not engage. If necessary, simply turn your back - or walk away.

title: Pride @ Work - Indy Pride Parade
description:
Pride at Work is a nonprofit organization that represents LGBTQ union members and their allies. We are an officially recognized constituency group of the AFL-CIO (American Federation of Labor & Congress of Industrial Organizations) that organizes mutual support between the organized Labor Movement and the LGBTQ Community to further social and economic justice. From our national office in Washington, DC, we coordinate and support more than 20 Chapters across the country.

We seek full equality for LGBTQ Workers in workplaces and unions. We work towards creating a Labor Movement that cherishes diversity, encourages openness, and ensures safety & dignity. We aim to educate the LGBTQ Community about the benefits of a union contract for LGBTQ working people, and to build support and solidarity for the union movement in the LGBTQ community.

We organize in the spirit of the union movement's historic motto, "An Injury to One is An Injury to All." We oppose all forms of discrimination on the job and in our unions based on sex, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, race, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, religion or political views.

title: Good Local News Panel: 4 outlets blooming in a hostile environment
description:
Despite the serious headwinds that the local news business is facing, there are many excellent state and local news outlets. 

**This panel will highlight four exceptional news organizations** that are prospering and finding new ways to cover their states, cities and towns — doing better than ever covering the diverse communities they serve. Their editors will discuss what they are doing to connect to their communities and to cover the news in these difficult times.

Our distinguished panelists are:

 - **Akash Mehta**, Editor-in-Chief of [New York Focus](https://nysfocus.com/author/akash/)
- **Donna Ladd**, Founder, ED and Editor of [Mississippi Free Press](https://www.mississippifreepress.org/listings/items/donna-ladd-2/)
- **Nina Misuraca Ignaczak**, Founder and editor of [Planet Detroit](https://planetdetroit.org/author/nina-ignaczak/)
-  **Angela Kuper Copeland**, Editor, [The Paper, Morganton NC](https://www.thepaper.media/)

**Stefanie Murray**, director of the [Center for Cooperative Media](https://centerforcooperativemedia.org/about/our-team/) will moderate the panel. 

Local news is a vital resource. Local journalists alert us to dangers, root out waste, and strengthen our communities. On top of all that, they make us better citizens. Studies show that civic engagement increases where local news is strong — more people vote.

Local news is particularly crucial in these difficult times. Among other things, the panelists will discuss how they are assessing the impacts of the MAGA cuts and how they are covering the growing movement to defend our democracy.

This event is co-hosted by the [Media and Democracy Project](https://www.mediaanddemocracyproject.org/journalism-directory) and [Markers For Democracy](https://markersfordemocracy.org/).

GRIT—Greater Rochester Integrity and Truth—is joining the national No Kings Day movement in a nationwide day of protest — and we’re taking it to the burbs. Join the Mayday Coalition Project on June 28th for an electrifying afternoon of protest and voter registration. We're carrying on the bold legacy of Stonewall by standing up to policies that are stripping away rights:

• The Trump Administration’s Trans Ban in the military.
• Ohio’s oppressive Drag Ban.
• The relentless rollback of LGBTQIA+ protections.
• Cuts to vital healthcare access for the LGBTQIA+ community.
• Expansions of religious exemptions aimed at denying LGBTQIA+ rights & services.
• The harmful measures of Project 2025.
• Rising discrimination in our workplaces and communities.

This isn't about starting something new—it’s about keeping the flame of freedom and equality burning strong. Your voice matters, your vote matters, and together we can ensure that the struggle for civil rights endures.

Are you ready to stand up and shout for change? Let's make history—because Stonewall was just the beginning.
